chapter_note: This chapter is nearly pure substrate — systematic cosmological teaching about the sea giant's formation and cosmic function. Teaching purity 0.936 is accurate. No editorial bridge, institutional, or exhortation vocabulary detected. The only non-substrate material is the single-line dialogue frame formula in paragraph 1. The teaching describes: (1) how the Living Spirit directed waste from the three vessels into the sea, explaining its salt and bitterness; (2) how the Father of Life purified the stellar sphere, casting sediment into the sea where it formed the sea giant bearing zodiacal impressions; (3) the three cosmic purposes of the sea giant — purifying the sphere, fettering the zodiac powers, and gathering all elements. Every mapping stays within the cosmic system. The craftsman analogy in paragraph 6 serves cosmic explanation, not contemporary application. This is one of the purest substrate chapters in the corpus.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic dialogue frame opening. 'Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples' — stereotyped attribution formula with no cosmological content.

paragraphs.core_text: After the Living Spirit constructed things and the worlds, he came up and set himself upon this earth. He gave a sign to the King of Glory, who turned the three wheels and caused the wheels that are found [ ... ] up above all the mountains; he spread forth the wind to them, he breathed on them, he stirred them up, he washed the earth with the waters. And the waste and the accretion of the three vessels, they of water and of Darkness and of fire, which had been discharged upon the earth, he gathered them and deposited them in the sea that is within the walls and the vessels; because of this sea waters are salty. For they have received salt and bitterness from the washing out and cleansing of the three vessels.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological process: Living Spirit → King of Glory → three wheels → washing earth → waste deposited in sea. Every entity and mapping is cosmic. The explanation of salt/bitterness is a classic correspondential teaching — physical quality mapped to cosmic process. High substrate vocabulary (13.24).

paragraphs.core_text: When the Father of Life came, rising in his ascent to the heights, he discharged the wheel of the stars; he washed it out and loosened all the sediment that was in it. He cast it down to this great inner sea like [ ... ] of the mountain. And that waste, the sediment of the washing out of the wheel, he cast it down and mixed it in with the sea waters. Its own thought collected it together; and the thought gathered the waste together in this way. It made it fast and fixed it [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic process continues: Father of Life purifies the stellar sphere by casting sediment into the sea. The 'thought' (of the waste matter) as an active agent collecting and fixing — this is the evil active thought that forms the sea giant. Purely cosmological, both sides internal to the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The sea giant had stamped upon him the seal of the seconds and the hours, the seal of the days and months and years, the impression of the stars and the signs of the zodiac [ ... ] He came into existence from them and was discharged from their power and cast into the sea. The images and the seals and aspects and doctrines and counsels of [ ... ] were sealed upon the body of that giant, because he is the residue of them all. Consequently, each star that will shine, and each sign of the zodiac that will turn: of one he shall be its inducement, and of another its confirmation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Zodiac-body correspondence teaching — the sea giant's body bears seals of temporal cycles (seconds, hours, days, months, years) and stellar/zodiacal impressions. This is the correspondential substrate at its purest: cosmic entity → temporal-astronomical correspondences. The 'inducement' and 'confirmation' describe the giant's functional relationship to stellar/zodiacal powers.

paragraphs.core_text: He was discharged into the sea like this, the way a cloud might discharge rainwater into the midst of the sea. They compelled him totally through the action of the power and the helmsmanship of the angels. He was swept down to the mill, the place where he was constructed in the setting up of the universe; and the sea also conceived him [ ... ] for its part [ ... ] it being his chief sculptor and chief craftsman. It sculpted him in a likeness, he being changed more than the other residue of the sea bodies.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological process: the giant's formation described through cosmic mechanics — 'helmsmanship of the angels', 'the mill' as the construction site, the sea as sculptor/craftsman. The cloud-rain simile is a natural illustration of cosmic process, not an application. 'Sea bodies' implies a class of cosmic entities formed in the sea.

paragraphs.core_text: This matter is comparable with a craftsman who might take the stamped impressions of many coins and cast them on the fire, and mould them [to a single] image. These thousands of impressions and thousands of shapes [are perfected] and make a single body [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching analogy explaining cosmic formation. The craftsman-coins simile illustrates how multiple stellar/zodiacal impressions were fused into the single body of the sea giant. Both sides of the analogy serve cosmic explanation — no reach into contemporary institutions. Zero substrate vocabulary score reflects absence of cosmic proper nouns, but the function is purely explanatory within the cosmic system. Integral to the teaching sequence (paragraph 7 explicitly ties it back).

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.115⟩
This is also the case with the sea giant, who too was moulded and sculpted by the power of the lust inside him from many doctrines and counsels that belong to the residue of the wheel of the sphere.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highest substrate score in chapter (27.5). Ties the craftsman analogy back to the cosmic entity. 'Lust' as active formative power, 'doctrines and counsels' as stellar properties, 'residue of the wheel of the sphere' — all cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text: The archetype of the giant was constructed for three things.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration header introducing the three-fold cosmic purpose of the sea giant. This is a structural teaching marker — it defines the framework for the following enumerated teaching (paragraphs 9-11). Brief but integral to the substrate structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The first: That the sphere would be relieved and purified of the burden present in it. In the same way that the ten firmaments were purified and relieved of the burden of the three vessels; so was it also done to the sphere, that it too might be relieved and purified of the burden and the waste inside it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumerated purpose. Systematic cosmic process: purification of the sphere, paralleled with purification of the ten firmaments from the three vessels. High substrate vocabulary (18.64). Classic degree-mapping: firmaments/three vessels paralleled with sphere/waste.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: That he might add a {fetter} and a prison to the wheel and the signs of the zodiac that are bound to it, so that when they wish to go up above, you can find the sea giant dragging them back as by an iron {fetter}, and they are unable to go up; and when the powers of the wheel would take a decision on a guileful thing, and it enters their mind to come down to the earth, they are not able to descend because of this stake that is nailed to the wheel upon the {} of the firmaments. This is one. However, this other one, because of its sleepless watchers that are set over it, it is turned all the time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumerated purpose. The sea giant as cosmic fetter binding zodiacal powers — preventing both ascent and descent. 'Iron fetter' is a metal-function correspondence. 'Stake nailed to the wheel', 'sleepless watchers' — all cosmic functional entities. The 'you can find' is a didactic address mode within the teaching, not editorial application. Two restraining mechanisms: the giant below, the watchers above.

paragraphs.core_text: The third thing: That the wind and the water and the fire that gush from the circuit of the sea, and the rivers that flow upon the face of the earth discharging into the sea, and the rainwaters that come to ground, and the waste and rebirth that come down to it; that sea will be a hostel and gathering place for all of these.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumerated purpose. The sea as cosmic gathering vessel for elements — wind, water, fire, rivers, rain, waste. All entities are cosmic/elemental. 'Hostel and gathering place' describes cosmic function. Zero substrate vocabulary score despite being clearly substrate — the vocabulary counter misses this because it uses natural-world terms (rivers, rain) rather than cosmic proper nouns, but the function is entirely cosmological.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.116⟩
As for all the power and the life that comes down to the sea, and in the breath that the sea giant will breathe and draw it into him that he might disturb the sea [ ... a] fullness and a [ ... ] becomes between his movement [ ... ] purify; but the sea [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily lacunose closing paragraph. What survives describes the sea giant breathing in life/power, and a purification process. Despite extensive lacunae, the surviving vocabulary is consistently cosmological — 'power', 'life', 'breath', 'purify'. The teaching appears to have described how life entering the sea is purified through the giant's activity, consistent with Gardner's synopsis.
